# Scheduling and Triggers

Covers dimensions 6 (Scheduling) and 8 (Webhook support). Sources referenced in
[citations.md](../citations.md).

---

## Scheduling (Dimension 6)

### Schedule Trigger

The Schedule trigger provides time-based flow execution (Agent B discovery,
verified against search snippets):

| Schedule Type | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| Cron | Quartz Scheduler cron expression format |
| Daily | Specific time each day |
| Weekly | Specific day and time |
| Monthly | Specific date and time |
| Hourly | Every N hours |

**Timezone handling:** Timezone is a required field for all scheduled flows
(Agent B discovery). Specific timezone support details (e.g., IANA timezone
database) were not extracted from the page — the Schedule piece page returned
only CSS content during WebFetch.

### Architecture

Schedule triggers create recurring jobs stored in Redis [4]. Failed jobs retry
automatically [4]. The trigger timeout is configurable via
`AP_TRIGGER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 60 seconds) [11].

### Trigger Failure Handling

`AP_TRIGGER_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` defaults to 576 consecutive failures before
disabling a trigger [11]. At a 5-minute polling interval, this represents ~2
days of continuous failure before automatic disable.

## Webhook Support (Dimension 8)

### Catch Webhook Trigger

External callers can trigger workflows via HTTP webhooks [13][16]:

| Property | Value | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| HTTP methods | GET, POST, PUT, DELETE | Agent B discovery |
| Max payload size | 5 MB | [13] |
| Sync response timeout | 30 seconds | [13] |
| Payload inline threshold | 512 KB (Redis), larger offloaded to file storage | [13] |
| Webhook timeout | Configurable via AP_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS | [11] |
| Max payload configurable | AP_MAX_WEBHOOK_PAYLOAD_SIZE_MB (default 5) | [11] |

### Authentication Options

| Method | Description | Source |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| None | Open endpoint | Agent B discovery |
| Basic Auth | Username/password | Agent B discovery |
| Header Auth | Custom header key/value | Agent B discovery |

**Gap:** HMAC authentication was requested but not yet implemented (Agent B
discovery). Bearer token authentication status unclear.

### Sync vs Async

- **Async (default):** Webhook returns immediately with 200 OK, flow executes
  in background
- **Sync:** URL ending in `/sync` waits for flow completion and returns the
  response, with 30-second timeout returning 408 if exceeded [13]

### Webhook URL Generation

Each flow with a webhook trigger gets an auto-generated URL via
`context.webhookUrl` (Agent B discovery). For self-hosted instances,
`AP_FRONTEND_URL` must be set for webhooks to be accessible [8][9].

---

## Assessment for Personal Assistant Use Case

**Scheduling: Meets requirements.** Cron expressions support the needed patterns
(daily, every 30 min, weekly Monday). Timezone handling is built in.

**Webhooks: Meets requirements.** HTTP-triggered execution with Basic Auth or
Header Auth provides sufficient security for a personal workstation. The PA can
trigger workflows via webhook URL without credentials.

**Caveat:** The personal workstation needs ngrok or similar for webhook
accessibility from external services, unless all triggers are schedule-based or
API-initiated from localhost [8][9].
